abstract:
The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no existing tool integrates them within a unified, reproducible framework.
We present hlafactor, a computational tool that brings together established HLA functional annotations within a single, standardised framework. Starting from two-field HLA genotype calls, whether imputed or molecularly typed, hlafactor assigns functional annotations from published reference datasets and applies established calculations to derive individual-level features. These include tapasin dependency scores, general and functional heterozygosity, allele-specific cell surface expression, NK cell-related polymorphisms (Bw4/Bw6, C1/C2, HLA-B -21 M/T), and class I/II supertype assignments. hlafactor also maps alleles to IMGT/HLA amino-acid alignments to generate residue-level genotypes. All outputs are formatted for direct use in downstream association analyses with existing software. Applied to 17,960 samples from the MalariaGEN consortium, each functional annotation module completed in under 15 seconds on a single CPU core, and preprocessing and quality control in just over four minutes, supporting its use in large cohort studies.
hlafactor is implemented in C ++20 and is freely available at https://github.com/QiJingS/hlafactor and archived on Zenodo under DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20647440.
